intended_object: A helper for one entry of a matrix in the congruence subgroup of I. It lifts the (i,j) entry of a matrix u ≡ 1 (mod I) to the element (δ_ij, u_ij − δ_ij) of the unitization ℤ ⊕ I. I inferred this from the docstring and from how the next definitions (`liftCongruenceMatrix` and the lemmas after it) use it.
explanation:
The definition is an auxiliary step in a proof. The library uses it to build the inverse of the map from GL_n(ℤ ⊕ I) (restricted to the augmentation kernel) to the congruence subgroup of GL_n(R) at I. On its own it is just a lift of one matrix entry, not a standard object from the literature.

The construction itself is correct. The first component is the identity entry δ_ij. The second component is u_ij − δ_ij, which lies in I by `congruenceSubgroup_entry_sub_mem`. Mapping this element back to R gives δ_ij + (u_ij − δ_ij) = u_ij, which is what the lemma `idealUnitizationToRing_liftCongruenceEntry` proves.
